Footprint lib:name: Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23-5 (KiCad default)
Notes/confidence: REPLACED the Microchip MCP1700T-3302E/TT on 2026-09-23. VERIFIED against the real TI data sheet SBVS277C (Jul 2019, rev Sep 2022). WHY: quiescent current drops from 1.6uA typ / 4uA max to 25nA typ / 46nA max at 25C (60nA max over -40..85C), and the MCP1700 was the single largest standby draw on a board that spends most of its life asleep. Board sleep current goes from ~4.3uA to ~2.7uA (-37%); the 2M R11/R12 sense divider at ~1.85uA is now the dominant term and is the next thing to gate. Shutdown IQ 3nA. 200mA rated vs 45mA worst-case load (4.4x headroom); current limit 450mA typ. VIN 1.5-6.0V covers the 3.0-4.2V battery rail. Accuracy +/-1.5% over temperature, better than the MCP1700's +/-2.5%. Dropout 270mV max at 200mA -> roughly 60mV at our 45mA, so the rail holds 3.3V down to ~3.36V in, about the same as the part it replaced. PSRR 55dB @1kHz, output noise 130uVrms, UVLO 1.3V rising. PINOUT IS NOT A DROP-IN: SOT-23-5 1=IN 2=GND 3=EN 4=NC 5=OUT (Table 5-1 / Figure 5-2) vs the MCP1700's SOT-23-3 1=GND 2=VOUT 3=VIN. EN HAS AN INTERNAL PULLDOWN AND THE PART IS DISABLED WHEN EN FLOATS, so EN is tied to VBAT -- it cannot be driven by a GPIO because the MCU this rail powers cannot enable its own supply. Pin 4 (NC) carries an explicit no-connect flag; the datasheet permits float or GND. Symbol is hand-authored and self-contained: KiCad ships no TPS7A02 at all, and every TPS7A05 sibling in Regulator_Linear is `extends`-based, which this repo forbids (kicad-cli silently reports an entire file as empty). Footprint is KiCad's stock SOT-23-5 -- NOT a placeholder.
